en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a perfectly symmetrical cone shape clearly observable from many surrounding towns.
Visitors can observe massive stalactites and stalagmites forming inside the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park.
The giant Rafflesia flower can be observed blooming on the dark forest floors of Mount Kitanglad in Bukidnon.
Philippine tarsiers, recognized by their unusually large eyes, can be observed clinging to branches in Bohol sanctuaries.
During the dry season, the grass covering the Chocolate Hills in Bohol turns brown, resembling chocolate mounds.
Visitors can observe a smaller volcano island and a tiny lake inside the main crater lake of Taal.
During the amihan season, Filipinos experience observable cool and dry northeast monsoon winds from November to February.
Tourists can observe natural sunlight illuminating the rocky walls of the main chamber in Cagayan's Callao Cave.
The striking blue water of the Hinatuan Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur is clearly observable from the surface.
Hikers can observe thick green moss completely covering the trees and rocks near the summit of Mount Pulag.
Crushed red corals mixed with white sand create the observable pink shoreline of Zamboanga's Great Santa Cruz Island.
Farmers carved massive, stair-like steps into the mountains of Ifugao, creating the highly observable Banaue Rice Terraces.
